news.headline: Intermountain Health Brings Perimeter's Claire™ to the Operating Room, a Landmark in Breast Cancer Surgery Using AI
news.summary: Intermountain Health became the first U.S. health system to commercially deploy Claire, now live at LDS Hospital and American Fork Hospital under a systemwide agreement covering 34 hospitals and 400 clinics. This is the first real commercial placement since March's FDA PMA approval, and shares jumped on the news.

news.headline: Perimeter Schedules Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Conference Call for August 20th
news.summary: Perimeter confirmed it will report Q2 2026 results after market close on Thursday, August 20, with a conference call and webcast at 5:00pm ET. This will be the first quarterly update covering commentary on the Intermountain Health launch and cash burn since the spring financings.

news.headline: Brookline Capital Markets Initiates Perimeter at Buy, PT C$1.54
news.summary: Analyst Kemp Doliver started coverage with a Buy rating and C$1.54 target (stock at C$0.32), citing Claire's Breakthrough Device status as a tailwind for a faster CMS New Technology APC reimbursement decision expected by year-end, and modeling over 9% lumpectomy penetration by 2035.

news.headline: Paradigm Capital names Perimeter and maintains Profound as healthcare Top Picks
news.summary: Paradigm Capital initiated Perimeter as a healthcare Top Pick with a Speculative Buy and a C$0.95 price target (stock at C$0.275 on July 3). The analyst frames the March FDA approval of Claire as the accelerant for U.S. commercialization and flags M&A optionality, noting the stock trades far below comparable MedTech takeout multiples.

news.headline: Perimeter Selected for INOVAIT Pilot Fund to Advance AI for Breast Cancer Surgery
news.summary: Perimeter secured up to ~C$148,000 from Canada's INOVAIT Pilot Fund plus C$100,000 in Mitacs funding to develop the next AI generation for Claire alongside the University of Toronto. The amount is small, but it is non-dilutive external validation of the AI platform.

news.headline: Perimeter Medical Imaging AI Closes Final Tranche of Non-Brokered Private Placement
news.summary: Perimeter closed the final tranche of its convertible-debenture placement, bringing the total to C$6.04M. Insider alignment was strong: CEO Mendes subscribed C$2.76M and Chamath Palihapitiya's SC Master Holdings (Social Capital) C$2.78M, though the notes add potential dilution.

catalysts.label: Q2 2026 financial results
catalysts.detail: Perimeter reports Q2 2026 results after market close on August 20 (two days from today), with a call/webcast at 5:00pm ET. Watch for the first commentary on the Intermountain Health commercial launch, new placements from the ~50-lead funnel, and cash burn versus the spring financings.

catalysts.label: Additional Claire hospital placements
catalysts.detail: With Intermountain Health now live as the first commercial deployment, the market is watching for additional U.S. hospital systems to sign on from Perimeter's pipeline of qualified leads in active Prospecting/Developing/Validating/Contracting stages.

catalysts.label: CMS New Technology APC / reimbursement decision
catalysts.detail: Management is pursuing a CMS New Technology APC / Category III T-code pathway for intraoperative AI-enabled OCT margin assessment, aided by Claire's Breakthrough Device Designation. Brookline Capital's July note flagged a CMS decision expected by year-end 2026; this remains a company/analyst target, not a confirmed CMS date, and would be a major driver of Claire's U.S. adoption economics.

catalysts.label: Possible Nasdaq up-listing
catalysts.detail: Cited by sell-side analysts as a potential catalyst to broaden U.S. investor access following FDA approval and commercial launch; no official timeline has been announced by the company.

pulse: Perimeter enters its August 20 Q2 2026 print on a high note: the August 13 Intermountain Health go-live was the first real commercial proof point since March's FDA approval, following back-to-back sell-side initiations in July from Brookline Capital (Buy, C$1.54 PT) and Paradigm Capital (Speculative Buy, C$0.95 PT) that both frame FDA clearance as the trigger for an accelerating U.S. adoption curve. With no material news since the August 13 double-header (deployment plus the earnings-date announcement), the market's attention is now squarely on Thursday's call for evidence of funnel conversion (roughly 50 qualified hospital leads), incremental placements beyond Intermountain, and cash runway following the spring convertible-debenture raise. Beyond earnings, the next structural catalysts are further hospital placements and a CMS reimbursement decision (New Technology APC) that analysts expect by year-end 2026, but the balance sheet still depends on further financing, so this remains a high-beta, news-driven micro-cap heading into a binary-feeling print.
